themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber, Lyft, etc.) spiked to 18 this week, up 860% from a baseline of 1.9 complaints per week over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a sudden operational or enforcement problem in Washington Heights/Inwood's transportation ecosystem.
evidence: 18 for-hire vehicle complaints this week vs. 1.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (860% spike, z-score: 12.71)
This represents the single largest percentage spike across all complaint categories tracked
Complaint type is narrow and measurable, indicating a concentrated problem rather than diffuse complaints
reporting_angles: Interview residents and merchants about specific complaints—illegal parking, double parking, aggressive driving, or congestion caused by for-hire vehicles
Reach out to TLC (Taxi and Limousine Commission) to determine if there's a known surge in service expansion, driver complaints, or enforcement actions in this district

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Safety Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 21 this week, up 380% from a 4.4-complaint weekly baseline, indicating rapid deterioration of pedestrian infrastructure in a neighborhood already requesting enhanced park safety.
evidence: 21 sidewalk condition complaints this week vs. 4.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (380% spike, z-score: 10.05)
Community board has repeatedly requested park safety enhancements, indicating pre-existing infrastructure concerns
Long-term pattern: Street Condition remains in top 10 complaint categories (633 complaints over 90 days), now accelerating acutely
reporting_angles: Walk and photograph the most complaint-heavy blocks in Washington Heights and Inwood to identify hazards (broken pavement, exposed utility lines, tree damage)
Investigate Department of Transportation and Parks Department backlog for sidewalk repairs—is there a staffing shortage or budget constraint?

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints surged to 3 this week from a 0.1 weekly baseline—a 2300% spike—coupled with a 319% surge in vendor enforcement complaints (11 this week vs. 2.6 average), suggesting either rapid vendor expansion or a failed enforcement response.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Concurrent 319% spike in vendor enforcement complaints (11 this week vs. 2.6 weekly average, z-score: 4.49)
Food poisoning complaints also up 400% this week (5 vs. 1.0 average)—possible hygiene connection
reporting_angles: Investigate whether a new vendor concentration or illegal vending operation has emerged near transit hubs or parks
Interview DOHMH and Department of Consumer Affairs about enforcement capacity and whether inspector staffing has changed

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Alarm
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints hit 5 this week, up 400% from a 1.0 weekly baseline, coinciding with the mobile food vendor spike and mobile vendor enforcement surge, raising questions about source and scale of a potential public health incident.
evidence: 5 food poisoning complaints this week vs. 1.0 weekly average (400% spike, z-score: 5.66)
Temporal correlation with 2300% mobile food vendor complaint spike and 319% vendor enforcement spike this same week
Suggests either a single source outbreak or systematic hygiene failures across multiple vendors
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) to request incident reports and environmental health investigation summaries for Washington Heights/Inwood this week
Interview residents and workers about symptoms, timing, and suspected food sources to narrow outbreak geography

themes_detail.label: Public Sanitation Degradation
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, complaints for unsanitary conditions (baseline), dead/dying trees (967% spike, 4 complaints), and water conservation issues (167% spike, 5 complaints) suggest environmental neglect; community board has repeatedly requested enhanced litter basket collection but issue appears to be worsening.
evidence: Dead/dying tree complaints: 4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% spike, z-score: 5.21)
Water conservation complaints: 5 this week vs. 1.9 weekly average (167% spike, z-score: 5.21)
Unsanitary condition remains top-5 complaint category (1,324 over 90 days); community board has requested more frequent litter collection multiple years running
reporting_angles: Map tree removal requests vs. actual removals to establish Department of Parks maintenance backlog in the district
Interview Department of Environmental Protection about water main breaks or conservation issues in the area
